name: @zebra-design-system/patterns
note: Generated when the patterns are packaged. Do not edit: change the .md files and package again.

entry.wants: get through a run of items, one after another
know whether things are all right
make something new, a step at a time
take something in from the world: a scan, a photo, a reading

recipes.title: Act on one object
recipes.summary: A screen about one thing: what it is, how it is doing, and what can be done to it.
recipes.job: Understand one object, then change it or act on it.
signals: One object's name is the page title.
Its status sits beside its name.
The content is facts about it, in groups.
chooseWhen: The person has already chosen the object.
The object has more to show than a row can hold.

instead.when: the object doesn't exist yet and takes several steps to make
the person is handling many objects in a row, the same way each time
the object is a group of other objects to look through

regions.name: Section navigator
regions.condition: the page has more than one section

variations.then: fields replace values in place; the layout stays as it is
each label sits above its value; the supporting pane moves below, or into a tab or sheet
the section navigator becomes a selector
reading content keeps a capped width; the supporting pane takes about a third on the trailing side
history is a section or tab, newest first

variations.when: AI has a finding about the object
variations.then: a decision card sits next to what it refers to

variations.when: the object can't be loaded, or the person may not see it
variations.then: a state block takes the place of the sections

spacing.between: a section heading and its facts

checks.check: Does the screen open with the object's identity, before any controls?
Is the status directly next to the name, in words?
Do the sections run in order of importance?
Does each action sit at the end of the section it acts on, with whole-object actions in the header?
Is there one primary action at most?
Do viewing and editing share one layout?

recipes.title: Capture
recipes.summary: Taking something in from the world: a scan, a photo, a reading.
recipes.job: Capture one thing correctly, see that it was taken, and move on.
signals: An instruction for what to scan leads the screen, or a camera view fills it.
The result appears where the person is already looking.
chooseWhen: The input comes from a scanner, a camera or a sensor.
The person's eyes are on the object, not the screen.

instead.when: captures repeat down a list of items

variations.then: a viewfinder takes the whole screen, with guidance over the top and the capture control at the bottom
results appear in a sheet over the image, which stays visible

variations.when: the process requires a scan as proof
variations.then: typing instead is not offered, and the screen says so
the on-screen primary keeps one position through the flow
the reason shows in place of the result, with how to try again

checks.check: Is the instruction for what to scan at the top of the content?
Does the result appear directly below it?
Is typing the value reachable on the same screen in one step?
Are the thing to look at and the thing to do the two most prominent elements?
Does a full-screen capture show how to leave?

recipes.title: Converse
recipes.summary: Asking in words and getting an answer, with a person or an AI assistant.
recipes.job: Ask, read the answer, and ask again.
signals: A composer is pinned to the bottom, or leads an empty screen.
Messages run above it, newest at the bottom.
chooseWhen: The person can't know in advance what they will ask.
The answer is read, then followed up.

instead.when: the task is narrow enough to be controls
AI is reporting a finding about something on another screen

variations.then: the composer is the most prominent block, with a greeting and suggestions directly above it
the answers lead; the composer stays pinned at the bottom
the composer is pinned to the bottom
submit becomes stop, in the same box
it shows inside the composer, with a way forward
more of the prompt becomes controls

variations.when: a suggestion starts an action rather than sending a message
variations.then: it looks different from one that sends

spacing.between: the latest answer and its follow-ups

checks.check: Is the composer always reachable?
Is the latest message directly above the input?
Does every mode of the composer happen inside the same box?
Does reading text keep a capped width on wide screens?
Can the person tell a suggestion that "says" from one that "does" before choosing it?

recipes.title: Create in steps
recipes.summary: Making something new, one step at a time, ending in a review.
recipes.job: Give everything a new thing needs, in an order that makes sense, then confirm it.
signals: A list or count of steps shows where the person is.
Back and Next sit together at the bottom.
The last step shows everything entered.
chooseWhen: The thing takes more inputs than a short task holds.
Later answers depend on earlier ones.

instead.when: it is one short decision or a few inputs
the steps are the same handling repeated on many items

variations.then: the step list sits at the leading side; the form keeps a capped width
the step list is a short "Step 2 of 5" label with the step's name
Next reads "Review"
Next becomes the finishing action, named for what it does
options are shown with a short description of each
an error summary appears above the form's heading
it asks first

spacing.between: one field group and the next
a group heading and its fields

checks.check: Does every step keep the same frame, with only the content changing?
Is the footer laid out the same on every step?
Is each step's title its heading?
Is the form one column, with a capped width?
Does the review show answers in the order and layout they were entered in, each with a way to change it?

recipes.title: Find one item
recipes.summary: A collection the person searches, filters and scans to reach the one item they came for.
recipes.job: Reach one item among many, then open it.
signals: A list, table or grid is the largest region on the screen.
Search or filters sit directly above it.
chooseWhen: There are more items than fit on one screen.
The person knows what they are looking for, or will know it when they see it.

instead.when: the person must handle every item in turn
the person wants to know what needs attention, not find a known item

regions.name: Search
regions.condition: finding by name is the main task

regions.name: Filters
regions.condition: the items differ in ways people narrow by

regions.name: Paging
regions.condition: people need to return to a place in the list

variations.then: a table becomes a list of rows; filters collapse behind one control that shows how many are active
the list stays beside the open item

variations.when: expanded width and many filter types
variations.then: filters move to a column on the leading side

variations.when: items are compared across several attributes
variations.then: the collection is a table, from medium width up
a selection bar replaces the header actions

variations.when: nothing matches, or it is loading or failed
variations.then: a state block takes the place of the collection; the header and filters stay

variations.when: creating an item is the screen's main action
variations.then: one create action, in the header or floating at the trailing bottom corner

checks.check: Is the identifier the first thing in every row?
Do search and filters sit directly above the results they change?
Is the result count between the filters and the first result?
Are active filters shown, each removable?
Do all rows share one anatomy and one height for the same kind of item?
When there are no results, are the header and filters still there?

recipes.title: Monitor
recipes.summary: A screen that shows whether things are all right, and what isn't.
recipes.job: See at a glance what needs attention, then go to it.
signals: A row of figures leads the screen.
Content is cards of charts, lists and counts.
Each tile or card opens the detail behind it.
chooseWhen: The person watches many things, and acts on few.
What matters is the exception, not the full list.

instead.when: the person is looking for one known item
everything shown is about one object

variations.then: the screen is visually quiet: no status colour
they take colour and the top position, by severity, then age

variations.when: the summary sits above a collection
variations.then: each status count filters the list below in place
cards run in one column; a chart that can't be read becomes its key figure and a list

variations.when: a card has no data, or failed
variations.then: a state block takes the place of that card's content only

spacing.between: a card's edge and its content

checks.check: Does the screen open with the few figures that matter most, in one row?
Are tiles in the row equal in size and anatomy?
Does each tile carry a comparison where one exists?
Is colour used only for exceptions?
Do all chart cards share one internal layout?
Does every tile and card open the list or detail behind it?

recipes.title: Work through many
recipes.summary: A run of items handled one after another, the same way each time.
recipes.job: Finish every item in a run: pick, count, check, deliver.
signals: One item fills the screen, with its position in the run.
One action finishes it and brings the next.
The same screen repeats for each item.
chooseWhen: Every item gets the same handling.
The order is given, or doesn't matter.

instead.when: the person chooses which item to open
handling each item means scanning or photographing it
the items are steps of one thing being made

variations.when: a hardware key does the primary action
variations.then: the on-screen primary sits in the same position on every screen of the run

variations.when: the item is confirmed by a scan
variations.then: a scan target leads the current item
the run's list stays beside the current item
a state block says so, with the way forward

spacing.between: Can't complete and the Commit bar

checks.check: Are the thing to look at and the thing to do the two most prominent elements?
Is the position in the run beside the current item?
Is the next item one action away?
Is "can't complete" set apart from the commit?
Does the primary action stay in one position from item to item?

organisms.name: Page header
organisms.job: Says which screen this is and holds the actions on the whole of it.

slots.holds: back, at the leading end
slots.condition: the screen is below the top level

slots.holds: the page title, at the leading edge
the object's status, directly after the title
slots.condition: the screen is about one object

slots.holds: page-level actions, at the trailing end

organisms.name: Identity block
organisms.job: Says which object this is, before any controls.

slots.holds: an image or a mark for the type of thing
the name people know it by
its status in words
the fact that tells it apart: serial, address, location

organisms.name: Fact grid
organisms.job: Read-only facts about one object, as pairs.

slots.holds: the kind of fact this group holds
slots.condition: there is more than one group

slots.holds: label and value, the value more prominent
the action on this group, at its end

organisms.name: Section navigator
organisms.job: Moves between parallel sections of one object.

slots.holds: one entry per section, the current one marked

organisms.name: Commit bar
organisms.job: Finishes what the person is doing, across exactly what it commits.

slots.holds: cancel, discard or the destructive action, at the leading end
how many and which it applies to
slots.condition: it commits across many objects or sites

slots.holds: the safe choice, then the commit last, at the trailing end

organisms.name: Search field
organisms.job: Finds by typing.

slots.holds: the field, saying what it searches
recent and suggested searches, before typing

organisms.name: Filter bar
organisms.job: Narrows the results directly below it.

slots.holds: named sets of filters, sort and columns
a few filter types, then "More filters"
the current sort, at the trailing end
removable chips with "Clear all"
how many results

organisms.name: Collection row
organisms.job: One item among many.

slots.holds: what kind of thing it is
which one it is: the identifier, then one or two lines
one status, value or affordance

organisms.name: Selection bar
organisms.job: Replaces the header actions while items are selected.

slots.holds: how many are selected
the actions that apply to all of them
cancel, or deselect all

organisms.name: Summary tile
organisms.job: One measure that matters, with what to compare it to.

slots.holds: what is measured
the figure
target, previous period or normal range
direction over time

organisms.name: Chart card
organisms.job: One chart, laid out like every other chart card in its set.

slots.holds: what the chart shows
the series, in the same place on every card
slots.condition: there is more than one series

slots.holds: the chart
a link to the detail behind it

organisms.name: Exception item
organisms.job: One thing that needs attention, in one line.

slots.holds: how severe it is
what it is, with the reason
the action or the value

organisms.name: Current item
organisms.job: The one item being worked on, in a run of many.

slots.holds: the item's identity
the facts being checked: location, quantity
where this is in the run

organisms.name: Step list
organisms.job: Where the person is in a fixed sequence.

slots.holds: completed, current and upcoming steps

organisms.name: Step footer
organisms.job: Moves through a sequence, with the same layout on every step.

slots.holds: cancel or discard, at the leading end
the step before
the primary, at the very trailing end

organisms.name: Field group
organisms.job: Related fields under one short heading.

slots.holds: what the group is about
slots.condition: the form has more than one group

slots.holds: each one as label, hint, error, input

organisms.name: Review block
organisms.job: One step's answers, as they were entered.

slots.holds: the step's title
in the order and layout they were entered in
a way back to that step

organisms.name: Message list
organisms.job: A conversation, newest at the bottom.

slots.holds: earlier messages, scrolling above
the latest answer, with its feedback controls
suggested next questions

organisms.name: Composer
organisms.job: Where a person writes to another person or to an AI assistant.

slots.holds: the text being written
attachments and what is in view
what it acts on, with a clear default
slots.condition: there is more than one scope

slots.holds: the kind of answer wanted
send, which becomes stop while generating
a few starting points, next to it

organisms.name: Scan target
organisms.job: What to scan, and what was scanned.

slots.holds: what to scan, at the top
the scanned value, directly below
a way to type the value

organisms.name: Viewfinder
organisms.job: A camera view that holds the whole screen.

slots.holds: the camera image
what to line up, over the top of the image
the capture control, at the bottom
how to leave

organisms.name: Decision card
organisms.job: AI output outside a conversation, next to what it refers to.

slots.holds: that this came from AI
the finding
why, with the evidence
one primary action

organisms.name: State block
organisms.job: Stands in for content that is empty, loading or failed.

slots.holds: what is happening, or what went wrong
the way forward

spacing.between: an icon and its label; a label and its field
items in one group: fields in a section, rows of facts, buttons in a group
a heading and the content it heads
a container's edge and its content
cards or tiles side by side
the page's edge and its content

spacing.tight: `--space-2xs` under a label, `--space-xs` beside an icon. Inside a component, its own gap.
spacing.related: `--space-sm`, or `--space-md` between fields and between rows that are targets
spacing.heading: `--space-sm`
spacing.inset: `--space-lg`, or `--space-md` at compact width. Never less than `--space-card`.
spacing.page: `--space-page`. The size mode on the root changes its value with width.

organisms.page-header: Screen Header Bar on desktop, Top App Bar on mobile
organisms.identity-block: Compose: Avatar or Icon, a title, Status Label, secondary text
organisms.fact-grid: Compose: a grid of label and value text. No component.
organisms.section-navigator: Tab Bar. Select at compact width with many sections.
organisms.commit-bar: Compose: a pinned bar with Button. The commit is `flavour="primary"`.
organisms.filter-bar: Compose: Filter Chip, Dropdown for sort, Input Chip for active filters
organisms.collection-row: A Table row, or compose a list row. Card only when items differ in kind.
organisms.selection-bar: Top App Bar in its selection state on mobile. Compose on desktop.
organisms.summary-tile: Compose: Card with label, value and comparison text
organisms.chart-card: Compose: Card. No chart component yet. Report it as a gap.
organisms.exception-item: Notification Item, or compose: Icon Indicator, text, Button
organisms.current-item: Compose: Card with the item, its facts and its position
organisms.step-footer: Compose: a pinned bar with Button. Next is `flavour="primary"`.
organisms.field-group: Compose: a heading with Input, Select and the other field components
organisms.review-block: Compose: a heading, a fact grid and a text Button for Change
organisms.scan-target: Compose: instruction text, the result, and Input for typing instead
organisms.viewfinder: No component. Compose it full screen with Icon Button.
organisms.decision-card: Compose: Card. No AI mark yet. Report it as a gap.
organisms.state-block: Compose: Icon, text and Button. Progress Circle while loading.
